# Creating S3-objects in bipartite

Starting with version 3.0 the `bipartite`-package enables object-oriented programming (OOP) using the S3 system. To understand what that mean we will demonstrate the new functionalities with the aid of the dataset `Safariland`.

```{r, results = "hide", message = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
library(bipartite)
data(Safariland)
options(max.print = 10)
```

```{r}
class(Safariland)
```

As the output above indicates `Safariland` is now of typ `bipartite_web` in 
addition to the types `matrix` and `array`.

```{r}
str(Safariland)
```

So the dataset in its core is still an integer matrix of size $9\times 27$ with named rows and columns. From the help file, we know that the columns represent pollinators and the rows represent plant species. 

Sometimes, that's all the information available about a network. More often, however, additional information is available about individual nodes or the network as a whole. 

For example, the `Safariland` data has additional information about the plants and pollinators available. We stored this data in two separate CSV files and load those into the workspace as `data.frame` objects.

```{r}
plant_attributes <- read.csv("plant_attributes.csv", row.names = 1)
plant_attributes <- plant_attributes[rownames(Safariland), ]
plant_attributes
```

```{r}
pollinator_attributes <- read.csv("pollinator_attributes.csv", row.names = 1)
pollinator_attributes <- pollinator_attributes[colnames(Safariland), ]
pollinator_attributes
```

Now we can create a new `bipartite_web` object combining the interaction matrix with the details on the plants and pollinators as well as some meta information.

```{r}
Safariland.web <- bipartite_web(Safariland,
                                lower_attributes = plant_attributes,
                                higher_attributes = pollinator_attributes,
                                meta_attributes = list("type" = "pollination"))
print(Safariland.web)
```

`Safariland.web` could now be stored and shared as a single R object containing all relevant information on the dataset. 

# 3D (multi-layer) network objects

Version 3.0 also introduces simple multilayer bipartite networks. The S3-class for those is called `bipartite_webarray` and in its core represents a 3D-array, in which the third dimension represents the various networks. 

```{r}
dim(Safariland.web)
dim(vazarr)
warray <- bipartite_webarray(Safariland.web, vazarr)
dim(warray)
```

```{r}
print(warray)
```

```{r}
pollinator_attributes <- read.csv("pollinator_attributes.csv", row.names = 1)
pollinator_attributes
```

```{r}
local_higher_attributes <- list("Safariland.web" = NULL, "vazarr" = data.frame(id = 1:41))
warray <- bipartite_webarray(Safariland.web, vazarr,
                             global_higher_attributes = pollinator_attributes,
                             local_higher_attributes = local_higher_attributes)
warray
```

```{r,error=TRUE}
warray[1:2, , ]
warray[, 1:2, ]
```

```{r, error = TRUE}
warray2 <- bipartite_webarray(Safariland.web, vazarr,
                  #  local_higher_attributes = list("vazarr" = data.frame(id = 1:10)))
                   local_higher_attributes = list("vazarr" = data.frame(id = 1:10), "b", "c"))
bipartite_webarray(vazarr, Safariland)
```

# Accessing the attributes

```{r}
higher_attributes(Safariland.web)
lower_attributes(Safariland.web)
meta_attributes(Safariland.web)
```

```{r}
higher_attributes(Safariland.web)$Order
higher_attributes(Safariland.web)["Ruizantheda proxima", ]
```

For `bipartite_webarray` there is a differentiation between the global and local attributes. The global attributes can be accessed by simply calling `*_attributes`:

```{r}
higher_attributes(warray)
```

Acccessing the local attributes however requires the use of the `web_id` argument:

```{r}
higher_attributes(warray, web_id = "vazarr")
```

# Replacing / changing the attributes

```{r}
meta_attributes(Safariland.web)$start_year <- 1999
meta_attributes(Safariland.web)$end_year <- 2000
meta_attributes(Safariland.web)
```

```{r, max.print = 50}
higher_attributes(Safariland.web)$id <- 1:ncol(Safariland.web)
higher_attributes(Safariland.web)
```

# Subsetting
```{r}
Safariland.web[1:5, 1:3]
Safariland.web[1:5, 1]
Safariland.web[1:5, 1] <- 1:5
Safariland.web[1:5, 1, drop = F]
Safariland.web[1:5, 1, drop = T]
Safariland.web[5, 3, drop = T]
Safariland.web[5, 3, drop = F]
```


```{r bipartite_webarray subsetting, error = TRUE}
warray[, , ]
```

```{r}
warray
```
